issues.title: Resolve Instagram delivery sizes to legal MAI generation sizes
issues.body:
MAI-Image-2.6 constrains every request to `width >= 768`, `height >= 768`, `width * height <= 1048576`. Those three rules interact in ways that are easy to get wrong, and the failure mode is a 400 at generation time that costs a request from a 2-12 RPM budget.

Two traps that look fine until you try them:

- Instagram's story format is 9:16 = 0.5625. The largest legal pair at that exact ratio is 767x1364 — the width is one pixel under the floor, so it is rejected. The usable pair is 768x1365, cropped afterwards.
- Instagram's landscape format is 1.91:1. Reaching it with a height >= 768 would need a width of 1467, which busts the pixel budget. It is **not generable at all**; we generate 16:9 and crop.

The legal aspect band is **0.5626 – 1.7773**.

**Delivered**

| Format | Instagram | Generate at | Crop |
|---|---|---|---|
| portrait (feed default) | 1080x1350 | 912x1140 | no |
| grid (profile crop) | 1080x1440 | 885x1180 | no |
| story / reel | 1080x1920 | 768x1365 | yes |
| square | 1080x1080 | 1024x1024 | no |
| landscape | 1080x566 | 1365x768 | yes |

All of this lives in one place (`resolve_dimensions`) because scattered, it will be got wrong.

**Files**: `backend/app/imaging/dimensions.py`, `backend/tests/test_dimensions.py`

**Verified**: every format asserted against the raw constraints rather than hard-coded numbers; >99% of the pixel budget used in all five; upscaling capped at 1.45x.

issues.title: Enforce Instagram safe zones as hard gates
issues.body:
Meta unified the 9:16 safe zone across Instagram/Facebook Stories and Reels in March 2026 and moved it from fixed pixels to percentages, because there are too many live phone aspect ratios for fixed margins to work.

**Reels/Stories at 1080x1920**: top 14%, bottom 35%, left/right 6% — a usable box of only **950x979**.

The 9:16 numbers used are deliberately the *Reels* ones. Designing to the Reels-safe box means the asset also works as a Story; designing to the Story box and posting as a Reel loses the bottom 15%.

Content outside the rect is not "slightly cropped", it is **invisible** — covered by the caption tray, audio credit, follow button and engagement rail. So violations raise `SafeZoneViolation` rather than warning; warnings get ignored at volume.

Also implements `grid_bleed_band`: Instagram's profile grid crops to 3:4 while the feed shows 4:5, so composing on 1080x1440 and keeping critical content inside the centred 1080x1350 band is what stops posts looking decapitated on a profile page.

**Files**: `backend/app/imaging/safezones.py`

**Note**: this gate fired on its first real use — a logo anchored 5% from the canvas edge lands under the feed caption row. Placement is now derived from the safe rect, so compliance is structural rather than checked afterwards.

issues.title: Composite the brand logo deterministically, never generate it
issues.body:
A diffusion model produces a *plausible* logo, which is a wrong logo — subtly wrong letterforms that still ship. Worse, describing a mark in a prompt is asking the model to reproduce a trademark, which is one of the risks Microsoft's own responsible-AI notes call out for these models.

So the logo is **never** described to MAI and never passed through an edit pass. The model's only job regarding it is to leave the room. The real file is composited server-side: byte-exact, instant, free, and re-renderable the moment the brand updates its mark.

**Implemented**

- Knockout variant derivation (light / dark) preserving the source alpha mask
- Placement anchored inside the **safe rect**, not the canvas edge
- Contrast-aware variant selection from the mean luminance of the destination patch, in linear light per WCAG
- Scrim escalation when neither knockout clears 4.5:1. A scrim treats the *background*; a drop shadow on the mark is forbidden by most brand guidelines
- Never rotates, recolours, or non-uniformly scales

**Files**: `backend/app/imaging/compose.py`

**Worth knowing**: 50% grey looks like the hard case but is not — a dark mark reaches ~4.8:1 against it. The genuinely problematic band is narrow (around luminance 0.19, where white reaches ~4.35 and black ~4.34) and is covered by a test.

issues.title: Render Indic text with Chromium/HarfBuzz instead of Pillow
issues.body:
**This is the highest-risk part of the product, and the risk is specific: broken shaping still renders.** A detached matra or an unformed conjunct produces a perfectly valid PNG that passes every size and pixel check, and is illegible only to someone who reads the script.

`PIL.features.check("raqm")` returns **False** on the dev machine, so `ImageDraw.text` would silently emit unreordered, disconnected glyphs. Pillow is used for pixels only.

Chromium already carries HarfBuzz and ICU, is continuously tested against these scripts by a browser vendor, and provides CSS line breaking plus an in-page auto-fit loop. The same template can drive the frontend preview, so there is only one renderer to keep correct.

**Enforced in code, not left to templates**

- `letter-spacing: 0` for every non-Latin script — tracking pulls shaped clusters apart and visibly breaks conjuncts
- `font-synthesis: none` — faux-bold smears conjuncts
- Per-script line-height (Devanagari/Bengali 1.5, Tamil/Telugu 1.45) — Latin's 1.2 clips marks
- Words are **never** broken; the fitter shrinks type instead, because breaking an Indic word splits a consonant from its matra

**Verified**: shaping is proven *active*, not merely inky, by measuring a ligated conjunct against the same characters forced apart with U+200C ZWNJ. If GSUB were not running the widths would match. Covers Devanagari (क्ष, शुद्ध), Bengali (বিশুদ্ধ), Telugu (స్వచ్ఛ), plus i-matra reordering.

**Files**: `backend/app/imaging/overlay.py`, `backend/tests/test_overlay.py`, `backend/scripts/language_proof.py`

issues.title: Model language as (language, script, register) so Hinglish is first-class
issues.body:
Language is not one dropdown. On Indian Instagram a large share of real marketing copy is Romanised Hindi rather than Devanagari, because many people speak Hindi fluently but read Devanagari slowly. Romanised output is a first-class variant, not a fallback.

Hinglish is simply `hi` + `Latn` + `conversational`.

v1 locales: English, Hindi, **Hinglish**, Marathi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu.

Also carries the per-script typographic metrics (font stack, line-height, minimum legible size, letter-spacing lock) and a `length_factor` used to scale English character budgets — Indic runs 15–40% longer for the same meaning, and Tamil (1.35) is routinely the one that overflows.

**Files**: `backend/app/copy/languages.py`

issues.title: Build the MAI prompt with a pure function, not an LLM
issues.body:
The LLM produces structured semantics (a `CreativeBrief`); a pure function turns semantics into prompt text. That gives diffable prompt versions, reproducible renders, and — most importantly — a place to enforce clauses that must **never** be dropped by a model having a creative moment.

**The two load-bearing clauses**

1. *No text*, enumerated. Diffusion models trained on advertising imagery have a strong prior to add lettering; "no text" alone reliably still produces signage and watermarks. The clause names text, lettering, words, numbers, letterforms, signage, watermark, logo and typography.
2. *Reserved negative space*, so the logo and every language's copy have somewhere to land.

**Global prohibitions** that exist for legal rather than aesthetic reasons: any map (a diffusion-drawn map of India gets the boundaries wrong), any national flag, any recognisable public figure, any third-party trademark.

Also provides `render_edit_prompt` for the image-to-image path. MAI's edit mode explicitly supports *text updates*, meaning it will happily re-letter packaging it is shown — so "keep my product, restage the scene" has to forbid that explicitly.

**Files**: `backend/app/copy/strategy.py`

issues.title: MAI-Image-2.6 client with rate limiting and 429 backoff
issues.body:
The only place in the codebase that talks to MAI. Isolated because these models are **public preview**: no SLA, and the API surface may change.

**API shape** (verified against Microsoft Learn)

```
POST {endpoint}/mai/v1/images/generations   JSON
    {model, prompt, width, height, auto_aspect_ratio, web_grounding}
POST {endpoint}/mai/v1/images/edits         multipart/form-data
    model, prompt, image=<JPEG|PNG>
-> {"data": [{"b64_json": "<base64 PNG>"}]}
```

`width`/`height` are parameters of the **generations endpoint only**. The edits endpoint takes no dimensions, so output geometry is handled by cropping either side of the call, never by asking the API.

**Implemented**: Entra ID (`DefaultAzureCredential`) or API key; token bucket defaulting to 2 RPM; full-jitter exponential backoff honouring `Retry-After` as a floor; bucket drain on 429 so the burst allowance is not spent on further rejected requests; dimension pre-check so a bad size fails locally instead of costing a request.

**Not retried**: 400/401/404 are our own bugs (bad dimensions, bad credentials, wrong deployment name) and retrying them burns quota we do not have. Each gets an actionable message.

**Files**: `backend/app/foundry/image_client.py`, `backend/app/foundry/ratelimit.py`

⚠️ **Never exercised against the live endpoint.** See the Phase 2 issue.

issues.title: Mock image backend so the pipeline is buildable without Azure
issues.body:
There is no local emulator for MAI, and the real deployment allows 2-12 requests per minute. Without a mock the pipeline could not be built or tested before Azure exists, and the test suite would inherit a rate limit.

The mock honours the parts of the contract the rest of the pipeline depends on: returns a PNG, at exactly the requested dimensions, and **refuses dimensions MAI would reject** — so a dimension bug fails in tests rather than in production. Output is keyed off the prompt hash, so the same brief always renders the same placeholder and visual diffs stay meaningful.

Its `edit()` deliberately ignores any requested size and follows the input, mirroring the real endpoint, so callers cannot accidentally depend on behaviour that does not exist.

`MAI_MOCK` defaults to **on**. A test asserts it stays on, so the suite can never quietly start spending real quota.

**Files**: `backend/app/foundry/mock_client.py`

issues.title: Campaign pipeline: one image generation, N language variants
issues.body:
The shape of this module is the whole architectural argument:

> **ONE image generation per format → N language variants, composited.**

The generation is the only call that touches MAI's 2-12 RPM budget. Everything after it is CPU work that scales freely, which is what makes the seventh language cost nothing and the seventh *format* cost a generation.

**Measured on the demo campaign: 2 image calls → 14 deliverables.**

Copy is generated *first*, because it costs no image quota — a failure there should not burn a generation, and having it ready lets the UI show progress while the image is still queued.

Also handles the reference-image path: cover-crop the reference to the target aspect going in (the edits endpoint takes no dimensions) and crop whatever comes back on the way out.

Every variant carries a `needs_review` flag with reasons — broken words, type below the legible minimum, unreviewed machine-written copy, or a rejected logo placement.

**Files**: `backend/app/pipeline.py`

issues.title: Job-based API and campaign bundle export
issues.body:
Generation is never synchronous. MAI allows 2-12 requests per minute and a single render takes tens of seconds, so a request that waited for an image would time out behind almost any proxy. Every generation is a job; the client polls.

**Endpoints**: `GET /healthz`, `GET /api/meta`, `POST /api/campaigns` (202), `GET /api/jobs/{id}`, `GET /api/jobs/{id}/bundle`, `POST /api/uploads/logo`.

`/api/meta` exposes the generation size for each format so the frontend reads dimensions from the server rather than duplicating the rules client-side.

**The export is a bundle, not an image.** A marketer needs the creative *plus* the caption, hashtags, CTA, alt text and the English back-translation, per language — and a `REVIEW.txt` listing anything not ready to publish. Shipping a single-image download would be a demo, not a product.

Uploaded logos are re-encoded on the way in, which normalises the format and strips EXIF or any embedded payload from a file we did not create.

**Files**: `backend/app/main.py`, `backend/tests/test_api.py`

issues.title: Transcreation copy layer (stub writer)
issues.body:
Each locale is authored from a shared `CreativeStrategy`, never translated from the English output.

Translating finished English copy produces text that is accurate and dead — and worse, it carries the wrong cultural referent. A Diwali line translated into Bengali is still a Diwali line, when the campaign that audience responds to is **Durga Puja**. Authoring per language from a strategy lets the referent change, not just the words. `occasion_by_locale` makes that substitution explicit, and the stub demonstrates it.

**Implemented**: `CreativeStrategy`, `BrandKit` (deliberately small — onboarding over ~90 seconds is where users drop out), `LocaleCopy`/`CopyPack`, the full transcreation prompt for a Foundry chat model, and a `StubCopyWriter` returning realistic canned copy so the pipeline is exercised honestly.

Every locale requests **three headline length variants**, so the typesetter *selects* a line that fits rather than shrinking type below legibility.

Every locale carries an English back-translation and starts `needs_review=True`. For the scripts with no OCR coverage that flag is the only gate between a model and a published brand asset.

The AI-disclosure line is part of the caption in each language, because platforms strip metadata on upload and the caption is the only disclosure channel that reliably survives.

**Files**: `backend/app/copy/transcreate.py`

**Pending**: the live model. See the Phase 2 issue.

issues.title: Wire the live Foundry chat model for transcreation
issues.body:
Copy currently comes from `StubCopyWriter` — canned strings with the right shape. Replace it with a real Foundry chat deployment implementing the same `CopyWriter` protocol.

The transcreation prompt is already written in `backend/app/copy/transcreate.py::build_prompt`; it carries the strategy, brand voice, per-locale occasion, and grapheme-cluster character budgets.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Deploy a chat model and add `MAI_TEXT_DEPLOYMENT` to config
- [ ] Implement `FoundryCopyWriter` with JSON-schema structured output
- [ ] Separate deployment from the image model so a copy burst cannot starve image quota
- [ ] Validate returned character budgets server-side, counting grapheme clusters not code points
- [ ] Back-translate each locale and flag semantic drift

**Acceptance**: a campaign in all 7 locales with no stub involvement; budgets respected; the Bengali occasion substitution still happens.

**Note**: verify which chat models are actually deployable in `southindia` before choosing one — do not architect on a model that needs a gated-access application.

issues.title: OCR gate: assert the generated base image contains no text
issues.body:
The prompt forbids text exhaustively, but a prompt is advisory. Diffusion models trained on advertising imagery add lettering anyway — a hallucinated "SOLE 50% OFFF" on a shop sign behind the subject is the single most common thing that makes AI creative unusable.

**Gate**: run OCR on every base image and assert **zero** text regions above a confidence floor. On failure, re-render once with a strengthened clause, then fall back to inpaint-removal via `/mai/v1/images/edits` ("remove all text and lettering, keep everything else identical") — which is exactly the documented artifact-cleanup capability.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Wire Azure AI Vision Read
- [ ] Add the gate to the pipeline between generation and compositing
- [ ] Unicode-block histogram on any OCR output to catch stray hallucinated glyphs
- [ ] Surface failures in the review queue rather than silently retrying forever

**Acceptance**: a base image containing text never reaches compositing.

**Constraint worth restating**: Azure Read supports Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic and Devanagari, but **not** Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Gujarati, Gurmukhi or Odia. This gate therefore protects the *base*; it cannot validate model-drawn text in most of our languages, which is precisely why we never let the model draw them.

issues.title: Azure AI Content Safety at every checkpoint
issues.body:
Four checkpoints, because the raw model output is not the artifact:

1. **Input brief** — Analyze Text + Prompt Shields + blocklists
2. **Uploaded reference image** — Analyze Image, plus OCR of any text in it fed to Prompt Shields as `documents[]` (a reference image containing "ignore previous instructions" is textbook indirect injection)
3. **Raw MAI output** — Analyze Image; discard on block, never persist
4. **Final composited creative** — Analyze Image again. **This is the one teams forget.** Compositing changes meaning: benign imagery plus a headline can become a violating creative

**Known weakness to design around**: Content Safety is optimised for nine languages and merely "functional" in many more. For all our target languages except English, severity scoring is less reliable. Mitigation: moderate both the native-script copy *and* its English back-translation, and take the max severity.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Wire the four checkpoints
- [ ] Per-tenant blocklists (competitors, banned claims)
- [ ] Block taxonomy with specific, non-preachy user messages — never a generic "something went wrong"
- [ ] Never auto-sanitise-and-retry an injection; that trains users to iterate on jailbreaks

issues.title: C2PA provenance and AI-disclosure labelling
issues.body:
**This is law, not guidance.** MeitY's IT Amendment Rules took effect 20 Feb 2026: synthetically generated *visual* content must be clearly labelled, with provenance metadata embedded where feasible. AI-generated *text* is excluded. Instagram, as a significant intermediary, must require users to declare AI content at upload.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Attach a C2PA manifest at the compositing step, signed with our own certificate. Compositing modifies pixels, so any inherited manifest is invalidated anyway
- [ ] Write IPTC `DigitalSourceType = trainedAlgorithmicMedia` and XMP — far more platforms read IPTC than parse C2PA
- [ ] On-creative disclosure badge, positionable and brand-styled; default ON for photorealistic human imagery and regulated categories, OFF for abstract/typographic
- [ ] Store full lineage server-side regardless: brief hash, model + version, prompt, safety verdicts, font versions, brand-kit version. Provenance you control beats provenance you hope survives a re-encode
- [ ] Tell the user Instagram will ask them to declare AI content, and that the honest answer is yes

The per-language caption disclosure line is **already implemented** in `transcreate.py` — platforms strip metadata on upload, so the caption is the only channel that reliably survives.

**Open question**: whether MAI output already carries Content Credentials is undocumented (it is documented for Azure OpenAI image models, silent for MAI). Probe with `c2patool` before claiming it does.

issues.title: Category compliance gates for Indian advertising
issues.body:
Position this as *"we catch the obvious problems and tell you what to check"* — a checklist plus an audit log, not a legal opinion. Keep the rules as updatable configuration, not code: ASCI's AI-labelling guidelines and SEBI's advertisement code were both still in draft as of September 2026.

**Gates**
- [ ] **Food/beverage** — FSSAI licence number field; flag unsubstantiated superlatives **in every language** ("100% शुद्ध" must be caught too)
- [ ] **Financial** — mandatory risk disclaimer; block returns/guaranteed-profit claims and synthetic-human endorsement of specific products
- [ ] **Alcohol/tobacco** — block outright in v1. Surrogate advertising rules are contradictory across instruments and not worth the exposure
- [ ] **Pharma/health** — block disease-cure claims; block synthetic doctors, lab coats, stethoscopes
- [ ] **Real estate** — mandatory RERA registration number, auto-placed fine-print band
- [ ] **Coaching/education** — flag rank and selection claims; require consent confirmation for student imagery

**ASCI risk tiers** map onto product behaviour: high risk (deepfakes, fabricated authority figures) is a **hard block — a label does not cure these**; medium risk defaults the label ON; low risk defaults it OFF.

Have Indian advertising counsel review the rules table before launch.

issues.title: Hard blocks: maps, flags, deities, public figures
issues.body:
Currently these appear only as prompt text in `GLOBAL_PROHIBITIONS`. A prompt is advisory; these need enforcement at the input and output ends too.

**Never generate, no override**
- **Maps of India** — the model will render an incorrect boundary for J&K/Ladakh/Arunachal. Publishing one is a legal and PR problem. Substitute a single vetted vector asset
- **The national flag** — governed by the Flag Code. No distortion, no use as drapery, no placement on disposable items. This goes wrong around 15 August and 26 January. Use a vetted asset
- **Deities on products, footwear, apparel, floor surfaces, or discarded packaging**, or adjacent to alcohol, tobacco, beef or leather
- **Public figures, celebrity likenesses, fabricated authority figures**
- **Skin-lightening / "fairness" claims** in any language

**Gate with confirmation**: deity imagery in a festive context (Lakshmi/Ganesha at Diwali is normal and widely used, but must be respectful and not for a restricted category); religious attire; anything targeting children.

**Representation defaults**: unprompted, the model will produce a light-skinned, thin, 22-year-old woman every time. Expose a skin-tone control defaulting to a realistic Indian distribution, and flag gender-role defaults in the prompt-expansion layer.

**Tasks**
- [ ] NER on the brief to catch named people and third-party organisations
- [ ] Blocklists: Indian public figures, major trademarks, per-brand competitors
- [ ] Vetted asset library for flag and map
- [ ] Vision check on output for third-party marks

issues.title: Persistent job store, real state machine, and SSE
issues.body:
Jobs currently live in a module-level dict and vanish on restart. That is fine for the vertical slice and not fine once a job can sit in a queue for minutes behind a 2 RPM limiter.

**Tasks**
- [ ] SQLite via SQLAlchemy, schema written Postgres-shaped for a later lift
- [ ] Explicit state machine: `queued → preflight → generating → rate_limited → postprocessing → compositing → safety_review → complete`, plus `failed`, `cancelled`, `blocked`
- [ ] Append-only `job_events` table driving both SSE and the audit trail
- [ ] Idempotency key per job so a client retry never double-spends a model call
- [ ] Admission control: reject with an honest ETA when `queue_depth / RPM` exceeds a threshold, rather than accepting work we cannot do
- [ ] SSE at `/api/jobs/{id}/events` with 20s keep-alives — **polling stays the source of truth**, SSE is a latency optimisation

**Acceptance**: 10 concurrent jobs at `MAI_RPM=2` complete with no 429 reaching the user and no lost jobs across a restart.

issues.title: Reference-image path in the API with both sub-modes
issues.body:
The pipeline supports a reference image, but the API does not expose it. This is half the product's stated input surface.

**Two sub-modes, surfaced explicitly** because they behave very differently:

- **"Use as inspiration" (default)** — a vision model extracts a style profile (lighting, palette, surface, camera, prop density), then the *text* path runs. Output obeys our layout, aspect ratio and safe zones
- **"Edit this image"** — goes to `/mai/v1/images/edits` directly. Requires an explicit rights attestation checkbox

Default to inspiration and require an affirmative signal for edit mode. The legal exposure differs: edit mode derives the output pixel-for-pixel from the input, so if the user uploaded a competitor's ad it produces a derivative work.

**Worth building early**: *"Keep my product, restage the scene"* — a fixed edit skeleton pinning product fidelity while mutating only background and lighting. It is the highest-value operation for an Indian D2C seller with a real phone photo, and `render_edit_prompt` already implements the product-fidelity clause.

**Tasks**
- [ ] `POST /api/campaigns/{id}/reference` upload
- [ ] Intent classification to pre-select the mode from the user's phrasing
- [ ] Rights attestation captured and stored
- [ ] Vision model for the style-profile extraction

issues.title: Bundle Noto fonts, pin versions, add golden shaping tests to CI
issues.body:
Rendering currently falls back to Windows' **Nirmala UI**, which covers every v1 script and is fine for development — but it is **not redistributable**, and it is not what will be installed on a Linux container.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Bundle Noto Sans Devanagari / Bengali / Tamil / Telugu (SIL OFL) in `fonts/`
- [ ] **Pin exact versions and hash them.** A silent Noto upgrade changes line metrics and reflows every historical creative
- [ ] Stamp `render_engine_version` on every variant so a Chromium upgrade is detectable
- [ ] Golden-image suite per script, with the conjunct torture strings already used in tests (क्ष्म्य, ஸ்ரீ, স্ক্র, స్వచ్ఛ, stacked matras)
- [ ] Run the suite in CI and fail on drift

The ZWNJ width comparison already proves shaping is *active*; goldens catch the subtler regression where shaping is active but the font changed underneath.

**Acceptance**: rendering is identical on Windows dev and a Linux container, and a font or engine change fails CI rather than shipping quietly.

issues.title: Native-speaker review workflow
issues.body:
Every machine-written locale is currently flagged `needs_review=True` and the bundle carries a `REVIEW.txt`. There is no way to actually *do* the review.

This matters more than it sounds: for Bengali, Tamil and Telugu we have **no automated verification of rendered text at all** (Azure Read does not support those scripts). The honest answer to "how do you know the Tamil is right?" is *deterministic font rendering plus human review of a sample* — so the review path has to exist.

**Tasks**
- [ ] `PATCH /api/campaigns/{id}/copy/{locale}` with `review_state: approved`
- [ ] Approved copy is never auto-regenerated
- [ ] Show the English back-translation alongside, so a reviewer who cannot read the script can still check meaning
- [ ] Block export of unreviewed copy for regulated categories
- [ ] Per-language acceptability sampling before GA

**Never report an average across languages** — it hides the case where one language is failing badly.

issues.title: React frontend with Instagram phone-frame preview
issues.body:
No frontend exists yet.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Vite + React + TypeScript
- [ ] Structured brief form (product, offer, occasion, audience, objective, tone) — **not a bare prompt box**. Marketers write bad prompts; do not make them
- [ ] Brand kit onboarding in under 90 seconds, with colour auto-extraction from the uploaded logo
- [ ] Language picker exposing the (language, script, register) triple, with **Hinglish as a one-click preset**
- [ ] Live WYSIWYG preview reusing the *same* HTML overlay template the server renders from, so there is no second implementation to keep in sync
- [ ] **Phone-frame preview with safe-zone guides** for feed, grid and story. Marketers will not trust an output they cannot see framed in an actual Instagram UI
- [ ] Editable text before export — non-negotiable
- [ ] Job progress showing queue position, with copy appearing while the image is still rendering

Read formats and locales from `GET /api/meta` rather than duplicating the dimension rules client-side.

issues.title: Route drafts to MAI-Image-2.6-Flash
issues.body:
`MAI-Image-2.6-Flash` has the same documented capabilities as 2.6 at lower cost and latency, and — critically — **a separate deployment gets its own RPM bucket**. Routing drafts there roughly doubles usable throughput.

The client already takes a `draft: bool` and a `MAI_DRAFT_DEPLOYMENT` setting; nothing uses them yet.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Deploy `MAI-Image-2.6-Flash` alongside 2.6
- [ ] Expose Draft / Final in the API, not the model name — users should never pick a model
- [ ] Draft grid at 768x768 for concept selection, final at max legal pixels for the chosen format
- [ ] Separate token buckets per deployment

**Verify first**: that separate deployments really do get independent RPM allocations. The whole benefit rests on it.

issues.title: Economy mode: one 9:16 master cropped down to every other format
issues.body:
Each format currently costs its own generation. Cropping a tall image to any wider ratio is free, so a single 9:16 master can yield 3:4, 4:5 and 1:1 at **zero** extra model calls — turning a 4-format campaign from 4 calls into 1.

**The trade-off is real and should be a user-visible toggle, not a silent default**: the master is 768px wide, so a 4:5 crop upscales ~1.41x rather than ~1.18x, and composition control is weaker because the subject must sit inside a band that survives every crop.

**Tasks**
- [ ] `economy: bool` on the campaign request
- [ ] Generate the 9:16 master and derive the rest via `grid_bleed_band`-style centred crops
- [ ] Brief the negative space so it survives every crop
- [ ] Show the quality trade-off in the UI

Keep per-format generation as the quality default while volume is low.

issues.title: Azure infrastructure as code
issues.body:
Everything currently runs locally against SQLite and the filesystem. The `az` commands for the Foundry resource are documented in the README but nothing is codified.

**Target topology**
- Container Apps (HTTP-ingress API + queue-driven worker, scale-to-zero)
- PostgreSQL Flexible Server (Burstable for dev, General Purpose with zone redundancy for prod)
- **Service Bus, not Storage Queues** — duplicate detection gives idempotency free, scheduled delivery gives 429 backoff free, dead-lettering gives poison handling free
- Blob Storage with user-delegation SAS, private containers, Shared Key disabled
- Front Door Standard + WAF (Azure CDN classic is retiring and blocked for new profiles)
- Managed identity end to end; **no API keys in production**

**Tasks**
- [ ] Bicep for all of the above
- [ ] Transactional quota decrement so concurrency cannot overshoot spend
- [ ] Azure Budgets with an automated kill switch flipping the worker to mock mode — and test the kill switch before it is needed
- [ ] Data residency in an India region; MAI is available in `southindia`

**Note**: Container Apps caps HTTP requests at 240s, which is another reason generation is a job rather than a synchronous call.

issues.title: Festival calendar presets
issues.body:
The Indian marketing year is festival-driven, and a marketer's actual planning question is never "what image should I make" but **"what am I posting for Navratri?"**

A preset is: occasion + palette + motif set + copy angles + language/region default + compliance flags. Selecting **Onam** should suggest Malayalam and pookalam/kasavu motifs, and must *not* offer diyas.

**Regional coupling is the whole point** — Pongal is Tamil Nadu, Onam is Kerala (a bigger commercial window there than Diwali), Durga Puja is West Bengal, Bihu is Assam, Ganesh Chaturthi is Maharashtra. The April regional new years are seven different festivals in one fortnight.

`occasion_by_locale` already exists in `CreativeStrategy` and is the hook for this.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Calendar as a primary navigation surface, not a template category
- [ ] **Do not hardcode dates** — they shift with the lunar calendar; use a maintained feed and re-verify annually
- [ ] Warn on mismatches (Pongal + pan-India audience; Diwali + a Kerala audience)
- [ ] Pre-generate festive base plates offline during low-traffic hours — this is also the rate-limit strategy for the October–November crunch
- [ ] Lead-time nudges at T-45/T-21/T-7; festive creative is briefed 3–6 weeks ahead

issues.title: Carousel and WhatsApp Status formats
issues.body:
**Carousel** — cover + 4–6 content slides + CTA slide, as a consistent design system rather than N unrelated images. Slide 1 needs ~8% clear on the right for the swipe affordance and slide-count pill.

**WhatsApp Status** — 9:16, same asset as the story but a *different* safe zone (no bottom UI stack, so more usable height). India-specific and high value: Indian SMBs live on WhatsApp — briefs arrive there, approvals happen there, assets get sent there.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Carousel slide templates driven by the existing layout spec
- [ ] `whatsapp_status` format with its own insets in `safezones.py`
- [ ] "Send bundle to WhatsApp" export target

Both reuse the existing base image, so neither costs additional model calls.

issues.title: Brand kit CRUD with logo variants and colour extraction
issues.body:
`BrandKit` exists as a dataclass constructed per request; there is no persistence, and the logo upload endpoint just drops a file in a directory with no association to a brand.

**Minimum viable brand kit** (deliberately small — onboarding beyond ~90 seconds is where users drop out):
1. One logo file, plus auto-derived knockout variants (already implemented in `compose.derive_variants`)
2. Two brand colours + one CTA accent, **auto-extracted from the logo on upload** and confirmed by the user — this removes the biggest onboarding drop-off
3. A font pair from a curated, Indic-capable library — not a free-for-all upload
4. Brand name and handle
5. Three tone words, picked from chips rather than free text
6. One optional mandatory line

**The value of the brand kit is that off-brand output becomes impossible.** Lock the palette, lock the type, lock logo position to a few presets. A user who wants freeform design has Canva.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Persist brand kits and logos; cache trim bbox and mean luminance at upload
- [ ] k-means palette extraction from the logo
- [ ] Associate uploads with a brand instead of globbing the uploads directory

issues.title: Probe the open questions against a live MAI deployment
issues.body:
`MaiImageClient` is written but has **never been exercised against the real endpoint** — mock mode is on by default and a test asserts it stays on. These cannot be answered from the documentation and need a deployment.

- [ ] **Latency** at 1024x1024 for 2.6 vs 2.6-Flash. The entire interactive UX budget depends on this and the docs give no figures
- [ ] **C2PA**: does MAI output carry Content Credentials? Documented for Azure OpenAI image models, silent for MAI. Check with `c2patool` — do not assume
- [ ] **Content filter**: can a custom filter configuration attach to a `--model-format Microsoft` deployment, or is it default-filter-only as with GPT-image-1?
- [ ] **RPM buckets**: do separate draft/final deployments each get their own allocation? The Flash routing strategy depends on it
- [ ] **Edits output geometry**: the endpoint takes no width/height — confirm output follows the input, which is what the mock assumes
- [ ] **Translator transliterate** coverage for `ta` and `te` (`GET /languages?scope=transliteration`), needed for romanised variants

**Also on day one**: file the quota-increase request. Priority goes to customers actively using existing quota, so generate steadily from the start.

**Acceptance**: one real generation at 912x1140 that decodes, matches the requested dimensions, and passes the text-free check.

issues.title: Cache generated images so a repeat request is never paid for twice
issues.body:
Image generation is the dominant cost in the system and the quota is small, so the same request must never be billed twice.

Users re-click Generate constantly - while waiting, after a page refresh, after a restart. Without a cache each of those is a fresh charge for a byte-identical result.

**The key covers everything that changes the output**: prompt, model, dimensions, draft flag, and the 2.6-only flags. It deliberately does **not** include a timestamp or a seed, so a repeated request is a hit rather than a new variation. Wanting a different result is an explicit action (`bypass_cache=True`), never an accident of impatience.

Deliberately **not** a semantic cache. Two briefs being 95% similar does not mean the user wants the same picture - that is a correctness bug dressed up as an optimisation.

Writes go to a temp name and are then moved, so a crash mid-write cannot leave a truncated PNG that later reads as a valid hit.

**Files**: `backend/app/foundry/cache.py`

**Verified**: survives a restart; draft and final never share an entry; edits are keyed on the input image bytes; the same prompt at a different size is correctly a miss.

issues.title: Hard spend ceiling, enforced before the call and persisted
issues.body:
The failure this exists to prevent is not a user generating too much - it is a retry loop, a runaway test, or a queue bug quietly spending a month of credits in an afternoon.

So the limit is checked **before** the call, counted on disk so it survives a restart, and **refuses rather than warns**.

- Conservative defaults: 25/day, 200 total. Easier to raise a limit you hit than to un-spend a credit.
- **Failed calls are not counted.** A 429 or a network error costs nothing, so charging for it would make the ledger lie.
- The daily counter rolls over at midnight; the running total does not.
- A corrupt ledger starts fresh rather than crashing the service.
- Every call is appended to `usage.log` with what it was for, giving an honest per-campaign cost figure without waiting for the Azure bill.

Composed as `cache -> budget -> client`, so **a cache hit consumes no budget**. That ordering is the whole point and is covered by a test.

A refused call gets its own job state, `budget_exceeded`, distinct from `failed` - nothing is broken, we deliberately stopped short.

`GET /api/usage` reports spend, headroom and cache savings.

**Files**: `backend/app/foundry/budget.py`, `backend/tests/test_spend.py`

issues.title: Foundry provisioning and probe tooling
issues.body:
Two scripts so connecting Azure is minutes rather than an afternoon of copy-pasting CLI commands. Neither handles credentials - `az login` stays with the user.

**`scripts/setup_foundry.ps1`** provisions the resource group, Foundry resource, project and both deployments. It checks prerequisites first, and **confirms MAI-Image-2.6 is actually offered to the subscription before attempting a deployment** - these models are preview and access varies by account, so finding out at step 5 beats finding out halfway through. Prefers the version the service reports over the hard-coded guess. Supports `-WhatIf` and `-WriteEnv`.

**`backend/scripts/probe_foundry.py`** answers the questions in #29. Quota-aware by design: 3 image calls by default, reports exactly how many it used, and writes a report to paste into the issue. `--rpm-test` adds 4 more for the bucket-independence check.

Both guard against being run in the wrong state - mock mode on, or no endpoint configured - with a clear message rather than a traceback.

issues.title: Extract a reference image's style locally, with no model call
issues.body:
When a user says "make something like this", they usually mean the *look* - palette, lighting, whether it is bright and airy or dark and moody - not the literal subject.

All of that is measurable from the pixels: palette via quantisation, brightness and contrast from a luminance histogram, saturation and colour temperature from channel spread, orientation from the aspect. No model call, no quota, no latency.

A vision model would add richer description (camera angle, prop density, styling), but the expensive part is not the part that matters most - and under a credit constraint, paying to learn "this image is dark and warm" is the wrong trade.

Output reaches the prompt as **colour words, not hex codes**: diffusion models respond to "deep saffron" far better than to `#FF6B00`. The vocabulary is chosen for marketing imagery rather than completeness - words a photographer or art director would actually use, which is also what the model was trained on.

Nearest-colour matching weights the channels roughly by luminance contribution; plain RGB distance calls navy and forest green neighbours.

**It never extracts the subject.** Copying the silhouette of an image a user uploaded is how "inspired by" becomes a derivative work, so the reference's own silhouette, marks and faces go straight into `must_not_depict`.

**Files**: `backend/app/imaging/style.py`

issues.title: Drain in-flight jobs on shutdown
issues.body:
Background job tasks were fire-and-forget, so a shutdown could close the browser and HTTP client out from under a job still rendering into them. The job then awaited a page that would never respond - an indefinite hang, not an error.

Found by a test that started a campaign without awaiting it: the suite hung forever instead of finishing. Now 5 seconds.

In-flight tasks are tracked in a set; shutdown waits for them, then cancels whatever is left after a timeout. Real behaviour, not a test fixture - a deploy or a restart should not corrupt work in progress.

**Files**: `backend/app/main.py`

issues.title: Upgrade reference style extraction with a vision model
issues.body:
Local extraction covers palette, brightness, contrast, saturation, temperature and orientation. It cannot see **camera angle, lens feel, prop density, surface material, styling, or depth of field** - all things a user pointing at a reference often means.

A vision model returning a structured `StyleProfile` would. Worth doing once credits are less tight, and worth measuring against the local extractor rather than assuming it is better.

**Constraints that must carry over**

- Schema-constrained JSON output only. There must be no free-text field in which instruction text from an uploaded image could travel - a reference containing "ignore previous instructions" is textbook indirect injection.
- It must return `do_not_copy` entries for any identifiable silhouette, mark or face, exactly as the local extractor does.
- It must **not** extract the subject. That separation is what keeps this "in the style of".

**Do not make it a hard dependency of the render path.** Fall back to local extraction when the call fails or is slow; the product should degrade, not stop.

issues.title: Pre-select the reference mode from the user's phrasing
issues.body:
The two reference modes behave very differently and the user has to choose between them. A cheap classifier could pre-select the likely one so the common case is a single click rather than a decision.

- "remove the", "change the background", "make the sky", "keep the product" -> **edit**
- "like this", "similar vibe", "in this style", "inspired by" -> **inspiration**

**It must never override an explicit choice**, and it must never flip the default *to* edit without the user actively confirming - edit mode carries the rights attestation and the derivative-work exposure, so an inferred selection cannot be what unlocks it.

This is a UI affordance, not an authorisation step.

issues.title: Preserve the real subject through an edit (real estate, products, jewellery)
issues.body:
When a user uploads a photo of something they actually sell, the model must **restage** it, not **redesign** it.

This is not a quality preference. MAI's edit mode explicitly supports *text updates* and attribute changes, so left to itself it will re-letter a label, add a balcony, or turn a four-storey building into a five-storey one. For a property listing that is not a bad render - it is an advertisement for a building that does not exist, and the person running the tool cannot see the problem because the output looks excellent.

## Two mechanisms, because a prompt is advisory

**1. A clause that names the actual failures.** Generic wording does not work: a model told "keep the building the same" still changes the floor count, because it has no reason to think that is what "the same" means. So the clause enumerates per subject kind - for architecture that is floor count, every window, door and balcony, roofline, facade material, structural layout, railings and parapets, signage and unit numbers. Architecture gets an extra sentence: *this is a real, existing property and must remain recognisable as the same building*. Person gets one too - do not beautify, slim, lighten or retouch.

Eight kinds: architecture, product, food, apparel, jewellery, vehicle, person, generic.

**2. A measurement afterwards** that checks whether the model listened.

## Why it cannot be whole-frame similarity

The first implementation compared the frames directly and was **exactly backwards** - it rejected a legitimate sky change and passed an extra floor.

Restaging is *supposed* to change the background. Swapping a plain sky for a studio backdrop moves most of the pixels while leaving the subject untouched; adding a storey moves very few and destroys the listing's accuracy. Across the whole frame the harmless edit scores worse than the dangerous one.

So the subject is located first - it is the structured part of the image - and three things are measured: similarity inside the subject, change in its extent, and change in detail density inside that extent.

| Case | Similarity | Extent | Detail | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| identical | 1.000 | 1.00 | +0.0% | pass |
| sky recoloured *(legit)* | 1.000 | 1.00 | +0.2% | pass |
| bokeh background *(legit)* | 1.000 | 1.00 | +0.1% | pass |
| **one extra floor** | 1.000 | 0.78 | +0.0% | **reject** |
| **extra window per floor** | 1.000 | 0.77 | +0.0% | **reject** |
| **facade changed** | -0.092 | 0.74 | -87.2% | **reject** |

The extra floor scores **1.000 on similarity** - the original building is untouched, and only the extent signal catches it. One measure is not enough.

## Two subtleties that were bugs first

- **The structure threshold comes from the original only.** Deriving it per image means recolouring the sky moves that frame's statistics, moves its threshold, and silently reclassifies the building.
- **It is `mean + 2 sigma`, not a percentile.** The subject is usually a minority of the frame, so any percentile below ~0.9 lands inside the flat majority and the mask fills with noise. Measured: p75 was 4.5, well inside the flat region; mean+2sigma was 31.7, where the real window edges are.

## Behaviour

`subject_kind` is inferred from the brief when unset, but an explicit value always wins - the inference is a UI convenience, never the only safeguard. Preservation defaults **on**.

A failed check marks every variant for review rather than discarding the result: the marketer may look and accept it, but a drifted subject can never present itself as ready to publish.

**Files**: `backend/app/copy/fidelity.py`, `backend/app/imaging/fidelity.py`, `backend/tests/test_fidelity.py` (24 tests), [docs/fidelity.md](../blob/main/docs/fidelity.md)

**Not calibrated against real MAI output yet** - thresholds are reasoned, not measured. Expect tuning after #29.

issues.title: Calibrate fidelity thresholds against real MAI edits
issues.body:
Subject preservation is verified against **synthetic buildings only**. The thresholds - 0.92 similarity for architecture, 0.90 extent overlap, +/-15% detail density - are reasoned from what the signals mean, not measured against real model output.

Real photographs differ from the test fixtures in ways that matter: grain, compression, depth of field, and a subject that does not have crisp geometric edges. A restaging that is entirely acceptable may score lower than a synthetic one that is not.

**Tasks**

- [ ] Collect a small set of real edits: property exteriors, interiors, product shots, jewellery
- [ ] Score each, and have a human label whether the subject actually survived
- [ ] Plot the two against each other and move the thresholds to where they separate
- [ ] Check the false-positive rate specifically. Over-rejecting legitimate restaging would make the feature worse than not having it, because users learn to switch it off
- [ ] Re-check the dramatic cases: day to night changes facade tone legitimately

Depends on #29 for a working deployment. Until then the current thresholds are the honest best guess, and the failure direction is right - it flags for review rather than discarding.

issues.title: Zero-cost connection and resource discovery tooling
issues.body:
Connecting to Azure had to be cheap to get wrong, because the real probe costs images and a typo in an endpoint should not cost an image to discover.

**`check_connection.py`** verifies auth and deployment names with a **deliberately invalid request** - a width below the 768 floor, which the service rejects before generating anything. The status code still separates the three failures that matter: `401` bad key, `404` wrong deployment name, `400` both fine. Zero images.

It also detects the portal **project URL** being pasted instead of the host root. They look nearly identical and only one works, which is an easy hour to lose.

**`discover_foundry.ps1`** handles an existing resource rather than creating one. It answers the non-obvious question: MAI image models are preview and run only in `southindia` and `uaenorth`, so a perfectly healthy Azure OpenAI resource elsewhere simply cannot run them - and that failure surfaces as a 404 on the deployment name, which looks like a typo rather than a region problem. When the region cannot support it, the script lists the image models that *are* available there instead of just refusing.

Az calls go through a helper that keeps them quiet: PowerShell 5.1 turns a native command's stderr into ErrorRecords, so an expected failure like "not signed in" printed a wall of `NativeCommandError` noise over the actual message.

**It earned its keep immediately.** On first run it proved the endpoint and key were both valid while revealing that no MAI deployment existed - without spending anything.

**Files**: `backend/scripts/check_connection.py`, `scripts/discover_foundry.ps1`

issues.title: Cut the live probe to a single image
issues.body:
The probe was designed to cost 3 images. On a student subscription with limited credits for a showcase, that is the wrong default.

`--minimal` runs **one** image and still answers everything that could change the design:

- does it connect, and are dimensions honoured
- **real generation latency** - the number that decides whether the UI waits on screen or notifies, and which the documentation does not state anywhere
- **C2PA** - whether output already carries an AI-provenance certificate, which decides how much of #15 is actually needed

What it skips is comparisons rather than blockers: the Flash speed comparison and the edits-geometry check. Both can wait until they matter.

Also tightened the default ceilings for a student subscription: **5 images/day, 30 total**, down from 25/200.
